top_news.title: Delhi: Cabinet approves Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 under chairmanship of CM Rekha Gupta
top_news.summary: The Delhi government, under the leadership of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, has taken a step towards developing the capital into a clean, modern and technology-driven industrial hub. According to a press release, at a Cabinet meeting chaired by the Chief Minister on Tuesday, the Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 was approved. The policy aims to promote clean, high-value industries and knowledge- and technology-based businesses over the next 10 years. It provides for an expenditure of Rs 1,000 crore on the Mukhyamantri Udyamshree Yojana over five years, from the financial year 2026-27 to 2030-31. The objective is to encourage new industries and create more employment opportunities. CM Gupta said the Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 aims to position the capital as a major hub for advanced technology, Global Capability Centres, data centres, research and development, healthcare services, urban logistics, the circular economy and advanced manufacturing. The policy will promote clean, high-value industries, attract fresh investment, modernise existing industries, encourage women entrepreneurs and expand employment opportunities for young people, the release said. She said incentives would be tailored to the needs of the 10 priority sectors, covering capital investment, office or workspace rentals, new recruitment, research, certification, technological modernisation, energy efficiency and skill development. The policy will also encourage resource reuse and waste reduction. According to the release, a 25 per cent incentive on digital infrastructure investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available for three years. Office rental assistance of 40 per cent, up to Rs 2 crore, will also be provided for three years. Bandwidth and cloud services will qualify for 25 per cent assistance for two years, capped at Rs 10 lakh annually. An incentive of Rs 40,000 to Rs 50,000 will be provided for each new hire. A 25 per cent incentive on digital infrastructure investment, up to Rs 50 crore (Rs 60 crore for women), will be available for five years. Office rental assistance of 40 per cent, capped at Rs 2 crore, will be provided for two years. Each new hire will qualify for an incentive of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.2 lakh. The policy also provides 50% assistance for certification, up to Rs 25 lakh; a 30 per cent incentive for research and development, up to Rs 5 crore; and 25 per cent assistance for units developing workspaces, up to Rs 10 crore. A 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. The policy provides 30 per cent assistance for low-water-consumption cooling systems, capped at Rs 2 crore; 50 per cent assistance for certification and data security-related expenses, up to Rs 50 lakh; and 50 per cent assistance for regulatory compliance preparedness, up to Rs 25 lakh. The release added that a 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. Research activities will qualify for a 50 per cent grant, capped at Rs 50 lakh. Patent-related assistance will cover 25 per cent of the cost, up to Rs 5 lakh per patent, for a maximum of four patents. A 25 per cent incentive for laboratory accreditation-related expenses, up to Rs 25 lakh, will also be provided. A 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, generally capped at Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. Hospitals with 1,000 or more beds will be eligible for assistance of up to Rs 100 crore. Wellness activities will qualify for a 5 per cent incentive, up to Rs 1 crore, while certification by bodies such as NABH, NABL and JCI will receive 50% assistance, capped at Rs 20 lakh. Each new appointment of a specialist doctor will qualify for an incentive of Rs 50,000 to Rs 60,000. The release said that the new warehousing units will receive a 25 per cent incentive, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), while existing units will be eligible for 25 per cent assistance, capped at Rs 1 crore. Cold-chain facilities will qualify for a 25per cent incentive, up to Rs 2 crore. Technology adoption in logistics will receive 40 per cent assistance, capped at Rs 50 lakh, while the use of green energy will qualify for a 25 per cent incentive, up to Rs 2 crore. articles.title: Delhi: Cabinet approves Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 under chairmanship of CM Rekha Gupta
articles.summary: The Delhi government, under the leadership of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, has taken a step towards developing the capital into a clean, modern and technology-driven industrial hub. According to a press release, at a Cabinet meeting chaired by the Chief Minister on Tuesday, the Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 was approved. The policy aims to promote clean, high-value industries and knowledge- and technology-based businesses over the next 10 years. It provides for an expenditure of Rs 1,000 crore on the Mukhyamantri Udyamshree Yojana over five years, from the financial year 2026-27 to 2030-31. The objective is to encourage new industries and create more employment opportunities. CM Gupta said the Delhi Industrial Policy 2026 aims to position the capital as a major hub for advanced technology, Global Capability Centres, data centres, research and development, healthcare services, urban logistics, the circular economy and advanced manufacturing. The policy will promote clean, high-value industries, attract fresh investment, modernise existing industries, encourage women entrepreneurs and expand employment opportunities for young people, the release said. She said incentives would be tailored to the needs of the 10 priority sectors, covering capital investment, office or workspace rentals, new recruitment, research, certification, technological modernisation, energy efficiency and skill development. The policy will also encourage resource reuse and waste reduction. According to the release, a 25 per cent incentive on digital infrastructure investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available for three years. Office rental assistance of 40 per cent, up to Rs 2 crore, will also be provided for three years. Bandwidth and cloud services will qualify for 25 per cent assistance for two years, capped at Rs 10 lakh annually. An incentive of Rs 40,000 to Rs 50,000 will be provided for each new hire. A 25 per cent incentive on digital infrastructure investment, up to Rs 50 crore (Rs 60 crore for women), will be available for five years. Office rental assistance of 40 per cent, capped at Rs 2 crore, will be provided for two years. Each new hire will qualify for an incentive of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.2 lakh. The policy also provides 50% assistance for certification, up to Rs 25 lakh; a 30 per cent incentive for research and development, up to Rs 5 crore; and 25 per cent assistance for units developing workspaces, up to Rs 10 crore. A 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. The policy provides 30 per cent assistance for low-water-consumption cooling systems, capped at Rs 2 crore; 50 per cent assistance for certification and data security-related expenses, up to Rs 50 lakh; and 50 per cent assistance for regulatory compliance preparedness, up to Rs 25 lakh. The release added that a 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. Research activities will qualify for a 50 per cent grant, capped at Rs 50 lakh. Patent-related assistance will cover 25 per cent of the cost, up to Rs 5 lakh per patent, for a maximum of four patents. A 25 per cent incentive for laboratory accreditation-related expenses, up to Rs 25 lakh, will also be provided. A 25 per cent incentive on capital investment, generally capped at Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), will be available. Hospitals with 1,000 or more beds will be eligible for assistance of up to Rs 100 crore. Wellness activities will qualify for a 5 per cent incentive, up to Rs 1 crore, while certification by bodies such as NABH, NABL and JCI will receive 50% assistance, capped at Rs 20 lakh. Each new appointment of a specialist doctor will qualify for an incentive of Rs 50,000 to Rs 60,000. The release said that the new warehousing units will receive a 25 per cent incentive, up to Rs 10 crore (Rs 12 crore for women), while existing units will be eligible for 25 per cent assistance, capped at Rs 1 crore. Cold-chain facilities will qualify for a 25per cent incentive, up to Rs 2 crore. Technology adoption in logistics will receive 40 per cent assistance, capped at Rs 50 lakh, while the use of green energy will qualify for a 25 per cent incentive, up to Rs 2 crore.
